picked.t: Vietnamese duo quit $57,000 jobs to sell street food in Canada
picked.body: At lunchtime, nearly every red and blue plastic chair at their Toronto eatery is occupied. Customers chat while enjoying snacks such as mixed rice paper salad ( banh trang tron ), sweet soup che , and rice paper rolls ( banh trang cuon ). Vietnamese-language signs adorn the walls, recreating the atmosphere of casual street-side eateries in Ho Chi Minh City. Behind the business are Kim Ngoc and My Loan, both 29, who opened their first Premium Banh outlet in October 2024 using savings accumulated over years of working. By August 2026, they had their third outlet and around 20 employees. The duo moved to Canada in 2017 to study culinary arts. After graduating and gaining work experience, they met while working at a steakhouse in Toronto. Both grew up in HCMC and shared a fondness for Vietnamese street food. Whenever they craved a familiar dish, they would ask friends and relatives coming from Vietnam to bring rice paper. Their search for familiar flavors made them realize there was demand for Vietnamese street food in Toronto. Giving up stable jobs and good salaries to sell Vietnamese snacks was not an easy decision. "We figured that since we're still young, we might as well give it a try," they explain. In October 2024, they invested their savings to open their first outlet. "We want Vietnamese customers to rediscover familiar flavors and offer foreigners a chance to explore popular Vietnamese street foods," Ngoc says. Around 70% of their ingredients, including dried beef and dried shrimp, are imported from Vietnam, while fresh meat, vegetables, and eggs are sourced locally. The pair pay attention to small details to preserve the original flavors. For banh trang tron , for instance, they use kumquat instead of regular lime to achieve its characteristic sourness. A serving of mixed rice paper salad costs CAD13-14 (US$9.12-9.82) while other snacks range from CAD10-20; desserts and drinks are priced at CAD7-11. Building business from scratch The first 18 months were challenging. Ngoc and Loan took responsibility for almost every aspect of the business, from finding locations and renovating premises to sourcing ingredients, recruiting employees, managing finances, developing recipes, and monitoring food quality. The business initially brought in too little money, meaning the two were without a regular income to take care of their living expenses for a longish period. They relied on their savings and reducing their spending from around CAD4,000 each to CAD1,500. They also had to navigate Canadian business regulations and food safety standards while establishing a reliable supply chain for their ingredients. Loan recalls the difficult days: "There were times when the work left us completely exhausted; some nights, we barely slept at all. We just kept encouraging each other, reminding ourselves that even a small improvement over the previous day was a win." A turning point came last year when they took their food to a Vietnamese culinary festival in Canada. Their stall attracted long queues from the moment it opened comprising both Vietnamese expatriates and locals. Following the event, many visitors sought out their restaurant and recommended it to friends and family, helping the business build a stable customer base. Ngoc remembers one customer who tried banh trang cuon for the first time and was surprised by the combination of flavors. "She took a bite and exclaimed, 'Wow!'—she hadn't expected it to be so delicious. In the west, people are familiar with mango smoothies, but the idea of using mango inside rice paper rolls was completely new to them. When she learned the dish originated in Vietnam, she said, 'Oh my goodness, why didn't I discover this sooner?' She ended up coming back every single week." As the brand expanded to multiple locations, maintaining consistent food quality became another challenge. Ngoc and Loan developed standardized ingredient measurements, seasoning ratios and preparation procedures for every dish, particularly banh trang tron and their varieties of che . Their focus has shifted from establishing the business to building a sustainable Vietnamese food brand in Canada. "Rapid expansion is certainly welcome, but the most important thing is to maintain quality and a genuine passion for the food," the two add.

picked.t: Afghan visa overstayer in Vietnam faces prosecution for smuggling 56 compatriots into Cambodia
picked.body: The Ho Chi Minh City People's Procuracy recently issued an indictment prosecuting Mohammadi Mukhtar, 31, Du Duy Trung, 41, from Tay Ninh Province, and Le Dinh Chinh, 41, for organizing others' illegal exit from the country. The indictment says Mukhtar entered Vietnam from Cambodia through the Moc Bai International Border Gate in Tay Ninh on April 21, 2024, on a tourist visa valid until July 10 that year. He stayed on after it expired. During that time, he colluded with Trung and Chinh to send Afghans into Cambodia illegally through unofficial border crossings. Fee at every step In December 2024, Mukhtar agreed with a person named Ramozi Ahmad Hussain, whose background is unknown, to bring Afghans into Vietnam on tourist visas and then move them to Cambodia for VND7.5 million ($289) per person. For those without Vietnamese visas, Mukhtar passed their passport details and portrait photos to an unidentified woman who handled their tourist visa applications, at $150 per person. To get them across the border, Mukhtar struck a deal with Trung at VND4.5 million ($174) per person. Trung then hired someone named Hung, whose identity is also unknown, to take them across for VND2.5 million ($96) each, and hired Chinh to drive them for VND900,000 ($35) per person. Once the Afghans arrived in Vietnam, Mukhtar put them up in hotels and told Trung where they were. Trung then had Chinh pick them up by car and take them to the crossing area. From February to March 2025, the three organized illegal exits to Cambodia for 20 Afghans on four occasions. Between December 2024 and April 2025, they sent another 36 Afghans across through unofficial routes, but investigators could not establish who they were. Bank statements show Mukhtar received more than VND487 million ($18,800) in fees from the Afghans. On June 13, 2025, the security investigation agency of the Ho Chi Minh City Police ordered the arrest and detention of Mukhtar, Trung and Chinh for investigation.

picked.t: Vietnam's top leader to attend APEC summit in China
picked.body: The trip, running from Nov. 17 to 20, is at the invitation of Chinese Communist Party General Secretary and President Xi Jinping. The Vietnamese leader will be accompanied by his wife, Ngo Phuong Ly, according to a statement from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Since its founding in 1989, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum has established itself as the region's premier economic cooperation mechanism. It continues to spearhead efforts promoting economic, trade, and investment liberalization on both regional and global scales. These initiatives have contributed to economic growth, peace, stability, and development across the Asia-Pacific. APEC focuses on three primary pillars: trade and investment liberalization, business facilitation, and economic and technical cooperation. This final pillar emphasizes capacity building alongside equitable, sustainable development. The forum's 21 member economies represent approximately 37% of the global population, 62% of world GDP, and 48% of global trade. Vietnam joined the bloc in 1998. APEC members are vital to Vietnam's economy, bringing together 15 of the nation's 30 strategic and comprehensive partners. These economies account for more than 77% of Vietnam's overall trade, nearly 81% of its foreign direct investment, and over 85% of its tourism. Of the 19 free trade agreements (FTAs) Vietnam has either implemented or is currently negotiating, 13 involve APEC members. Seventeen of the forum's 21 members are Vietnam's FTA partners. China, the summit's host nation, holds deep historical ties with Vietnam. China became the first country to establish diplomatic relations with Vietnam, on Jan. 18, 1950. The two nations formed a comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership in 2008. In 2023, they issued a joint statement elevating this partnership to build a "Vietnam-China community with a shared future" carrying strategic significance. During To Lam's state visit to China in April, both sides released another joint statement pledging to further deepen this partnership in the new era. Economic ties between the two nations remain robust. In 2025, China stood as Vietnam's largest trading partner while Vietnam was China's top trading partner within ASEAN and its fourth-largest globally. Chinese investment in Vietnam is also substantial. As of late October 2026, China had over 7,487 active projects in Vietnam with total registered capital exceeding $38.15 billion. This places China sixth out of 154 countries and territories investing in the nation. Tourism figures further highlight this close relationship. Vietnam welcomed 5.28 million Chinese visitors in 2025, a 41.3% year-on-year increase. These visitors accounted for a quarter of all international arrivals, making China the largest source market for foreign tourists in Vietnam.

베트남 호치민시의 한 쌀국숫집에서 판매 중인 쇠고기쌀국수. 베트남 음식 11가지가 세계적인 미식 전문 매체가 꼽은 ‘아시아 100대 국물요리’에 이름을 올렸다. 글로벌 푸드 매거진 테이스트아틀라스(TasteAtlas)가 최근 발표한 ‘아시아 최고의 100대 국물요리(100 best soups in Asia)’에는 쇠고기쌀국수(Pho bo, 퍼보)를 포함해 베트남 음식 11종이 포함됐다. 테이스트아틀라스에 따르면, 이번 순위는 각 지역 미식 문화를 기념하고, 전통을 기리며 음식 애호가들로 하여금 새로운 맛을 탐험하도록 장려하기 위해 마련된 것으로, 전 세계 식객과 음식 전문가들의 리뷰 2만4,000여 개를 종합해 선정됐다. ◇ 퍼보 11위 퍼보는 소뼈와 사태, 꼬리, 목뼈 등을 넣고 오랜 시간 푹 고아낸 육수에 쌀국수 면을 담아낸 요리로, 계피와 팔각·정향 등 다양한 향신료가 더해져 독특한 풍미를 자아낸다. 일반적으로는 살짝 익힌 고기나 양지·사태·힘줄·미트볼 등 다양한 토핑을 선택할 수 있으며, 이 외 신선한 향채와 파, 칠리소스, 마늘 절임, 라임 등을 기호에 맞게 뿌려 먹는다. 호치민시 한 쌀국숫집에서 판매 중인 중부식 쌀국수 분보후에. ◇ 분보후에(Bun bo Hue) 26위 중부 고도 후에의 매콤한 쌀국수의 일종인 분보후에는 소뼈와 돼지뼈를 함께 우려낸 육수에 베트남식 새우젓(Mam tom)으로 간을 한 면요리로, 다른 베트남식 국수보다 맛이 강렬하고 복합적인 것이 특징이다. 분보후에는 궁중 요리의 영향을 받은 것으로 알려져 있으며, 깊은 맛으로 많은 미식가의 사랑을 받고 있다. ◇ 퍼가(Pho ga, 닭쌀국수) 33위 퍼가는 소고기가 부족하던 1930년대, 소뼈나 쇠고기 대신, 닭가슴살과 다릿살, 껍질, 지방 등 닭의 다양한 부위를 주원료로 만든 쌀국수로, 쇠고기쌀국수에 비해 육수가 한층 맑고 담백한 것이 특징이다. 퍼가의 육수는 생강, 느억맘(베트남 피시소스), 샬롯 등으로 풍미를 내며, 지역에 따라 다양한 향신채와 고명을 얹어 완성한다. ◇ 분리에우(Bun rieu, 민물게살국수) 38위 베트남 전통음식중 하나인 분리에우는 민물게를 껍질까지 갈아 만든 페이스트와 토마토를 뭉근하게 끓여낸 육수에 쌀가루를 주재료로 한 소면을 함께 내는 국수로, 신선한 게의 달큰한 맛과 토마토의 새콤한 맛이 조화롭게 어우러진 것이 가장 큰 특징이다. ◇ 채식쌀국수(Pho chay) 40위 채식 쌀국수는 쇠고기 또는 닭고기로 육수를 내는 일반적인 쌀국수와 달리, 각종 버섯과 생강, 양파, 간장, 그리고 정향과 계피 등의 향신료로 만든 육수에 숙주나물과 두부, 고추 등 갖가지 식물성 재료를 더한 음식이다. 토마토두부는 큐브 형태의 두부를 튀겨낸 다음 마늘과 샬롯, 고추, 토마토로 만든 토마토페퍼소스를 바른 것으로, 고수 등의 향채를 곁들여 먹는다. 이 밖에도 베트남식 핫팟(73위), 깐쭈아(Canh chua, 74위), 해산물쌀국수(75위), 후띠에우남방(Hu tieu Nam Vang, 87위), 반다꾸아(Banh da cua, 95위), 분망빗(Bun mang vit·오리국수, 100위) 등이 베트남 국물요리로 순위에 올랐다.
